items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: Well, Red, of course, was always a fine musician.

ctx.x: But, as you say, he's blending in with a lot of different --

Well, Red, of course, was always a fine musician. You know, people ask all the time, how does it happen that you can still play at this age and so on, well, I remember a few years before Coleman Hawkins died, I had an apartment in New York and he -- I didn't know this -- all these years was living just around the corner from me, and I saw him at a newsstand and I said, you know, we used to call him Bean, I said, Bean, why don't you come up to the apartment and have a little chat and have a drink. So he came up…

I remember asking him -- Hawkins was sort of a loner, but he was very nice to me. We got along beautifully, and I remember asking him, how does it happen that you and I, after all these years, are still in demand today.
